7. Mr. Ziaul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in support of the Rule submits that the facts and circumstances of the case, the suit land situated within Dhaka city can only be ascertained upon local investigation which can not be determined by oral or documentary evidence. He further submits that similarities and dissimilarities of demarcation of boundary in respect of the suit land can only be ascertained by local investigation by a survey knowing Advocate Commissioner. He next submits that the schedule to the plaint, being based on CS. and S.A. plot covering a big area, can not be ascertained without local investigation inasmuch as the lands in C.S. Plot has been divided into a number of plots. Without local investigation by survey knowing Advocate Commissioner it is not possible to determine the new plots under the city survey khatians. He further submits that as the suit land has not been demarcated on partition by mets and bounds it is not possible to ascertain and determine its identity and location without local investigation. He further submits the learned Judge of the appellate Court below without applying his mind judiciously to understand the spirit of local investigation as contemplated in Order XXVI Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure has illegally rejected the application of the petitioner praying for appointment of Advocate Commissioner for holding local investigation. He lastly that the impugned under has resulted in an error occasioning failure of justice which should be set aside. 

 10. Now I shall proceed with to examine whether the court of appeal below has rightly exercised its judicial mind in rejecting the application for appointment of an Advocate Commissioner for holding local investigation. The instant suit was for a decree of permanent injunction. In such suit the suit land must be specific and well identified as provided in Order VII Rule 3 of the Code. From the schedule appended to the plaint it appears the suit land measuring 11.50 decimals has been based on C.S. and S.A. Plot covering 6.46 acres of land situated within Dhaka City which has been divided into several plots and recorded in the Dhaka City survey khatians. Since the suit land covered by C.S. and S.A. Plots have not been identified by the R.S. and Dhaka City Survey khatians in the schedule of the plaint it is hardly possible to determine and ascertain the identity of the suit plot on the basis of oral and documentary evidence without holding local investigation by a survey knowing Advocate Commissioner. 

 "On perusal of the LCR it appears that schedule to the plaint does not contain the number of plot or khatians latest land survey which commonly called as City Survey." 

 From the observation quoted above it transpires that the suit land is not well identified by City Survey Khatian which can only be determined and ascertained on holding local investigation by a survey knowing Advocate Commissioner.
